subject: Hospitality
title: Menu Size: The Paradox of Choice
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Menu Size: The Paradox of Choice.

hook.text: The Cheesecake Factory has 250+ items. A Michelin-star tasting menu offers zero choices.

buildup.text: Psychologist Barry Schwartz found that too many choices cause decision fatigue.

discovery.text: Research suggests 7 items per category is optimal. More than 10 and decision quality drops.

twist.text: Large menus also increase waste—more ingredients, more spoilage, more prep. A 250-item menu demands massive inventory.

climax.text: Post-pandemic, many restaurants permanently shrank menus. Fewer items, better execution, lower costs, and happier guests.

punchline.text: 7 items per category, maximum satisfaction. Less choice means better decisions.

quiz.question: What is the optimal number of items per menu category according to research?
